questions.prompt: Make a sentence with a question tag.
questions.rule: A positive simple past sentence takes the tag didn't + pronoun: didn't he?
For an action happening now use am + verb-ing: I am doing.

options: Yes, I does. I play every Sunday.
Yes, I am. I play every Sunday.
Yes, I do. I play every Sunday.
questions.rule: Answer a tag question with the same helper: don't you? - Yes, I do.

questions.prompt: Change into the present continuous tense.
questions.source: The old man builds a bridge.
options: The old man is building a bridge.
The old man is build a bridge.
The old man are building a bridge.
questions.rule: Present continuous: is (for a singular subject) + verb-ing: is building.

options: You must not to waste time.
questions.rule: A modal is followed by the base verb without to: must not waste.
A positive sentence takes a negative tag with the same helper: can - can't she?

questions.rule: After Here the verb comes first and agrees with the subject after it. Grandpa is one person: Here comes.
Look! shows the action is happening now, so use the present continuous: are running.
should + base verb gives advice. ought needs to, and must never takes to.

questions.prompt: Make a sentence like a line of poetry.
questions.rule: Inversion: a place phrase first, then the verb, then the subject: Across the chasm walked a tired pilgrim.

chat: Do I need to bring my own lunch tomorrow?
options: No, you needn't to bring it.
No, you don't need bring it.
questions.rule: needn't is a modal, so the base verb follows without to. With don't need, you must add to.

chat: Your school bus is late today, isn't it?
options: Yes, it does. It usually comes at eight.
Yes, it is. It usually comes at eight.
Yes, it is. It usually come at eight.
questions.rule: isn't it? is answered with it is. A habit uses the simple present: it comes.

options: The pilgrim was tired, didn't he?
The pilgrim was tired, wasn't it?
The pilgrim was tired, wasn't he?
questions.rule: The tag repeats the helper (was - wasn't) and uses a pronoun for the subject: he.

questions.prompt: Find and fix the 2 errors in this paragraph.
questions.rule: Plural subjects take are + -ing (are flying); the continuous always needs the -ing form: is sitting.

options: Never again you will pass this way.
Never again will you passing this way.
Never again will you pass this way.
questions.rule: When a sentence starts with Never, the helper comes before the subject: will you pass.

questions.prompt: Pick the sentence with the correct tense.
options: We have been walk since morning.
We have been walking since morning.
questions.rule: An action that started in the past and is still going on uses have been + -ing with since.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: hardly makes the sentence negative, so the tag is positive: does she?

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: After a modal like needn't, use the base verb: needn't carry.
A suggestion with Let's always takes the tag shall we?

questions.prompt: Make a sentence in the present perfect continuous.
questions.rule: Present perfect continuous: has been + verb-ing, with since + the starting time.

chat: Why didn't you answer my call last night?
options: Sorry, I was having a bath when you called.
Sorry, I was have a bath when you called.
Sorry, I am having a bath when you called.
questions.rule: An action in progress when something else happened in the past: was + -ing: I was having a bath.

questions.source: I have never seen such a deep chasm.
options: Never have I seen such a deep chasm.
Never I have seen such a deep chasm.
Never have I see such a deep chasm.
questions.rule: After a starting Never, put the helper before the subject: Never have I seen.

questions.source: It is necessary for you to finish the work today.
options: You must finished the work today.
You must to finish the work today.
You must finish the work today.
questions.rule: It is necessary = must. A modal takes the base verb without to: must finish.

questions.prompt: Find and fix the 2 errors in this message.
questions.rule: You are takes the tag aren't you?; a Let's suggestion takes shall we?

options: A new bridge is been built across the river.
A new bridge is being built across the river.
A new bridge is building across the river.
questions.rule: Present continuous passive: is being + past participle: is being built.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: After Seldom the helper do comes first, and do is followed by the base verb: do we see.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: must has no past form. For a past need, use had to: Two days ago, Ravi had to leave.

questions.before: Nobody came to help the old man,
questions.rule: Nobody makes the sentence negative, so the tag is positive; the simple past uses did: did they?

questions.before: When the young pilgrim arrived, the old man
questions.rule: An action that went on for a time before another past action uses the past perfect continuous: had been building.

questions.prompt: Make a sentence about a possibility.
questions.rule: may + base verb shows something that is possible: may fall.

chat: You haven't seen my whistle, have you?
options: No, I haven't. Did you left it here?
No, I hasn't. Did you leave it here?
No, I haven't. Did you leave it here?
questions.rule: Answer with the helper from the tag: No, I haven't. After Did, use the base verb: leave.

questions.source: The old man is building a bridge.
options: A bridge is being built by the old man.
A bridge is built by the old man.
A bridge is been built by the old man.
questions.rule: Present continuous active becomes is being + past participle: is being built.

questions.source: The stream flowed down the hill.
options: Down the hill flowed the stream.
Down the hill did flowed the stream.
Down the hill flowed it the stream.
questions.rule: Put the place phrase first, then the verb, then the subject: Down the hill flowed the stream.

questions.prompt: Find and fix the 3 errors in this advice.
questions.rule: Modals take the base verb: should carry, mustn't walk, ought to take.

options: Little did the old man knows how much the bridge would help.
Little did the old man know how much the bridge would help.
Little the old man did know how much the bridge would help.
questions.rule: After a starting Little, use did + subject + base verb: Little did the old man know.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: Nobody is negative, so the tag is positive, and it uses they with were: were they?

questions.after: carry an umbrella; it isn't going to rain.
questions.rule: needn't = it is not necessary. As a modal it takes the base verb without to: needn't carry.
Never at the start: helper + subject + past participle: Never had the fellow seen.

chat: How long have you been learning the guitar, Aditi?
options: I have been learning it for two years now.
I am learning it for two years now.
I have been learn it for two years now.
questions.rule: How long have you been ...? is answered with have been + -ing and for + a length of time.

chat: Can I borrow your bicycle this evening?
options: Sure, but you must returned it by seven.
Sure, but you must to return it by seven.
Sure, but you must return it by seven.
questions.rule: must + base verb, with no to and no past form: must return.

options: Everyone enjoyed the trip, didn't them?
Everyone enjoyed the trip, didn't they?
Everyone enjoyed the trip, wasn't it?
questions.rule: Everyone takes they in the tag. A positive past sentence takes a negative tag: didn't they?

questions.source: The old man said, "I am building this bridge for him."
options: The old man said that he were building that bridge for him.
The old man said that he was building that bridge for him.
The old man said that I was building that bridge for him.
questions.rule: I becomes he, am building becomes was building, and this becomes that.

questions.prompt: Find and fix the 2 errors in this paragraph.
questions.rule: After inversion the helper still needs the past participle: had he seen, has a traveller taken.

questions.prompt: Find and fix the 3 errors in this message.
questions.rule: We are takes aren't we?; a length of time takes for; has needs the past participle: has seen.
